From detections to community analyses

Source: vignettes/community-matrices.Rmd
community-matrices.Rmd

Stage 3 of sheepdog turns the calibrated nightly detection history into site x month community matrices for multivariate analyses. This vignette runs that stage on the example data shipped with the package and closes with an illustrative ordination.

library(sheepdog)

The calibrated detection history

The example history is the output of calibrate() on simulated BirdNET predictions for four sites, five species and six months (October 2021 to March 2022), with five recorded nights per site x month, except for one recorder failure. In the simulation, occupancy is seasonal (higher in the rainy months, November to February) and differs among sites and species; the false-positive scores overlap those of true detections, at rates that vary among species and sites (data-raw/make_example_data.R).

ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog")
history_file <- file.path(ex, "nightly_detection_history.csv")
history <- readr::read_csv(history_file, show_col_types = FALSE,
                           col_types = readr::cols(night = "c"))
history
#> # A tibble: 579 × 10
#>    site  species night    n_detections n_reliable p_tp_max detection_k1
#>    <chr> <chr>   <chr>           <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>        <dbl>
#>  1 ARA   boa_ran 20211001            1          0   0.436             0
#>  2 ARA   boa_ran 20211016            1          0   0.425             0
#>  3 ARA   boa_ran 20211021            1          0   0.0658            0
#>  4 ARA   boa_ran 20211101           11          5   0.995             1
#>  5 ARA   boa_ran 20211106           11          5   0.996             1
#>  6 ARA   boa_ran 20211111           13          5   0.998             1
#>  7 ARA   boa_ran 20211116           17         12   1.000             1
#>  8 ARA   boa_ran 20211121            6          3   0.999             1
#>  9 ARA   boa_ran 20211201            9          3   0.997             1
#> 10 ARA   boa_ran 20211206            8          3   1.000             1
#> # ℹ 569 more rows
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: detection_k2 <dbl>, detection_k3 <dbl>, detection <dbl>

The history covers 4 sites (ARA, BAI, NHE, XAR) and 5 species (boa_ran, den_nan, lep_fus, pse_pla, sci_nas). Each row is a site x species x night. n_reliable counts the detections whose calibrated probability of being a true positive reached p_min in calibrate(); detection_k1 to detection_k3 flag nights with at least one, two or three such detections.

Why the entry rule must be strict

Occupancy models with false positives include an observation layer that absorbs misidentifications, provided that part of the detections are confirmed (see vignette("crywolf-integration")). Dissimilarity indices and ordinations have no such layer: a single false positive becomes a species “present” in a sample and contributes directly to beta diversity. community_matrices() therefore applies three filters.

  • Repetition rule (k_min). A species counts as detected on a night only when it had at least k_min reliable detections that night (column detection_k<k_min>). An isolated high-probability detection is more likely to be an error than repeated ones.
  • Core species. Only species whose calibration is reliable at every site enter the matrix. If the classifier has lower recall, or a poorer calibration, at some sites, the resulting differences in detection would appear as artefactual turnover among sites.
  • Minimum effort (min_nights_month). Each cell is the frequency of nights with detection, standardised by effort (nights with detection / nights recorded at that site x month). Cells with fewer recorded nights than min_nights_month give unstable frequencies and are dropped.

Choosing the core species

The choice of core species is made by the user, from the calibration diagnostics written by calibrate() (e.g. calibration_curves.png); the package does not make it automatically. summarise_history() gives a complementary view: the number of nights with a reliable detection per site and species under each repetition rule (shown below for k_min = 1).

by_site <- summarise_history(history)
by_site |>
  dplyr::select(site, species, nights_k1) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = site, values_from = nights_k1)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   species   ARA   BAI   NHE   XAR
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 boa_ran    25    30    30    23
#> 2 den_nan    30     8    15     8
#> 3 lep_fus     6     0     0     2
#> 4 pse_pla     0     0     0     0
#> 5 sci_nas     0     0     0     0

Species with no reliable detection anywhere (pse_pla, sci_nas) are cases in which calibrated probabilities rarely reach p_min, because their false-positive scores overlap those of true detections; in the simulation every species has a non-zero probability of occupancy at every site. Species reliably detected at some sites only (lep_fus) are the case the core rule targets: their absence from a site may reflect the classifier rather than the community. Here the core species are taken as those with at least one night with a reliable detection at every site (boa_ran, den_nan). This is a convenient proxy for the example; with real data the decision rests on the calibration diagnostics, and a species that is truly absent from some sites should not be excluded on this criterion alone.

core <- by_site |>
  dplyr::summarise(all_sites = all(nights_k1 > 0), .by = species) |>
  dplyr::filter(all_sites) |>
  dplyr::pull(species) |>
  sort()
core
#> [1] "boa_ran" "den_nan"

Building the matrices 

mats <- community_matrices(history, core_species = core, k_min = 2,
                           min_nights_month = 5)
names(mats)
#> [1] "frequency" "counts"    "effort"

The effort table lists the recorded nights per site x month and whether the cell entered the matrices.

mats$effort
#> # A tibble: 24 × 4
#>    site  month   n_nights_recorded included
#>    <chr> <chr>               <int> <lgl>   
#>  1 ARA   2021-10                 5 TRUE    
#>  2 ARA   2021-11                 5 TRUE    
#>  3 ARA   2021-12                 5 TRUE    
#>  4 ARA   2022-01                 5 TRUE    
#>  5 ARA   2022-02                 5 TRUE    
#>  6 ARA   2022-03                 5 TRUE    
#>  7 BAI   2021-10                 5 TRUE    
#>  8 BAI   2021-11                 5 TRUE    
#>  9 BAI   2021-12                 5 TRUE    
#> 10 BAI   2022-01                 5 TRUE    
#> # ℹ 14 more rows
mats$effort |> dplyr::filter(!included)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   site  month   n_nights_recorded included
#>   <chr> <chr>               <int> <lgl>   
#> 1 XAR   2021-10                 3 FALSE

Of the 24 site x month cells, 23 entered the matrices. The cell dropped by min_nights_month = 5 is XAR in 2021-10 (3 nights), the month of the simulated recorder failure; it remains listed in the effort table with included = FALSE. Effort is approximated by the number of distinct nights that appear in the history of the site for any species, which is adequate when detections are dense, as here.

The count matrix holds the number of nights with detection, and the frequency matrix divides it by the recorded nights:

mats$counts
#> # A tibble: 23 × 5

#> 10 BAI   2022-01                 5       5       0

mats$frequency

Sensitivity to the repetition rule

The repetition rule trades false positives against missed detections. The mean frequency of each core species across cells shows how the matrix changes with k_min:

sens <- lapply(1:3, function(k) {
  community_matrices(history, core, k_min = k)$frequency |>
    dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(core), mean)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(k_min = k, .before = 1)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
sens
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   k_min boa_ran den_nan
#>   <int>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     1   0.939   0.530
#> 2     2   0.870   0.287
#> 3     3   0.765   0.130

From k_min = 1 to 3, the mean frequency of boa_ran falls by 19%, whereas that of den_nan falls by 75%. The rule therefore acts unevenly among species, and its effect on the ordination should be reported. k_min = 2 is the default.

Writing the matrices to disk

build_community_matrices() is the wrapper that reads nightly_detection_history.csv, calls community_matrices() and writes the frequency and count matrices and the effort table as CSV files:

out <- file.path(tempdir(), "community_matrices")
mats <- build_community_matrices(history_file, out, core_species = core,
                                 k_min = 2, min_nights_month = 5)
#> Matrix: 23 rows (site x month) x 2 species | rule k >= 2
#> Effort: 23 site x month cells included; 1 dropped for having < 5 recorded nights (see effort_site_month.csv)
#> Files in: /tmp/RtmpZvY9vW/community_matrices
list.files(out)
#> [1] "count_matrix_site_month_k2.csv"     "effort_site_month.csv"             
#> [3] "frequency_matrix_site_month_k2.csv"

An illustrative ordination

The example has only 4 sites, six months and 2 core species, so the ordination below illustrates the workflow; it does not support inference. With so few species, the ordination adds little to a plot of the raw frequencies. It uses the vegan package, which is suggested but not required by sheepdog.

The dissimilarity is Bray–Curtis on the frequency matrix, which retains the quantitative information of the frequencies; Jaccard on incidence would discard it. [CITAR: properties of Bray–Curtis and Jaccard for frequency data in community ordination] Samples in which no core species was detected have undefined Bray–Curtis dissimilarity and must be removed first.

freq <- mats$frequency |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    season = ifelse(substr(month, 6, 7) %in% c("11", "12", "01", "02"),
                    "rainy", "dry"),
    label  = paste(site, month)
  )
Y <- as.matrix(freq[, core])
rownames(Y) <- freq$label
empty <- rowSums(Y) == 0
freq$label[empty] # samples removed
freq_ord <- freq[!empty, ]
Y <- Y[!empty, , drop = FALSE]
d <- vegan::vegdist(Y, method = "bray")

A principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) on the dissimilarity matrix:

pcoa <- vegan::wcmdscale(d, eig = TRUE)
expl <- pcoa$eig[pcoa$eig > 0] / sum(pcoa$eig[pcoa$eig > 0])
round(100 * expl[1:2], 1)
sum(pcoa$eig < 0) # negative eigenvalues
scores_pcoa <- data.frame(freq_ord[, c("site", "month", "season")],
                          PCo1 = pcoa$points[, 1], PCo2 = pcoa$points[, 2])

Bray–Curtis is not Euclidean, so some eigenvalues are negative; wcmdscale() returns only the axes with positive eigenvalues, and the percentages above are relative to their sum.

ggplot2::ggplot(scores_pcoa,
                ggplot2::aes(PCo1, PCo2, colour = site, shape = season)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = sprintf("PCo1 (%.1f%%)", 100 * expl[1]),
    y = sprintf("PCo2 (%.1f%%)", 100 * expl[2]),
    colour = "Site", shape = "Season"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()

Samples with identical frequencies share a single point. Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) on the same dissimilarity, with stress reported:

set.seed(2026)
nmds <- vegan::metaMDS(d, k = 2, trymax = 50, trace = FALSE)
nmds$stress
scores_nmds <- data.frame(freq_ord[, c("site", "season")],
                          vegan::scores(nmds))
ggplot2::ggplot(scores_nmds,
                ggplot2::aes(NMDS1, NMDS2, colour = site, shape = season)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::labs(colour = "Site", shape = "Season",
                caption = sprintf("Stress = %.3f", nmds$stress)) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()

The low stress is expected: 2 species define a low-dimensional configuration, and a two-dimensional NMDS reproduces it almost exactly.

A note on inference

A PERMANOVA (vegan::adonis2()) could test for differences between seasons, but the example does not support that test. There are only a few samples from 4 sites, and months within a site are not independent replicates: they share the site, its species pool and its recorder, and consecutive months are temporally autocorrelated. Restricting permutations to within sites (strata = site) respects the blocking by site but not the temporal dependence, and the cell dropped for low effort leaves the blocks unbalanced. The code is shown for completeness and its p-value should not be interpreted:

set.seed(2026)
vegan::adonis2(d ~ season, data = freq_ord, strata = freq_ord$site,
               permutations = 999)

A design that supports inference would need more sites per treatment, or a model that accounts explicitly for repeated measures within sites.
